extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: The WikiText language modeling dataset, introduced alongside the pointer sentinel mixture model paper. It is constructed from Wikipedia articles that meet Good or Featured article criteria, featuring punctuation, original casing, larger vocabularies, and numbers. Available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (approximately twice the size of Penn Treebank) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million words, featuring all extracted articles). Both datasets use the same articles for validation and testing. The dataset is designed to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
extraction.citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1609.07843.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia that fit the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text extracted from Wikipedia articles meeting Good or Featured article criteria, obtained via the Wikipedia API. Raw Wikipedia markup was processed to extract plain text.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Numbers were further split (e.g., 8,600 to 8 @,@ 600). Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to further split numbers and with some additional minor fixes. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3, following Chelba et al. (2013). Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token. The dataset was provided in the same format and following the same conventions as the Penn Treebank dataset.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), Wikipedia API
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling, enabling more realistic language modeling benchmarks compared to the Penn Treebank.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Articles are limited to those meeting Wikipedia's Good or Featured article criteria, which may introduce selection bias toward well-written and factually verified content. The dataset reflects the topics and perspectives covered by Wikipedia editors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Other larger scale language modeling datasets exist but either have restrictive licensing which prevents widespread use or have randomized sentence ordering which is unrealistic for most language use and prevents effective learning and evaluation of longer term dependencies. The Penn Treebank, by contrast, has tokens that are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words, making it unrealistic for real language use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling benchmark for training and evaluation, specifically designed to evaluate how well language models can exploit longer contexts and deal with more realistic vocabularies and larger corpora. Suitable for word-level language modeling tasks. WikiText-2 is intended for smaller-scale experiments and WikiText-103 for larger-scale experiments.
